subject: Altitude & Decompression
stem: A 34-year-old pilot reports tingling and lightheadedness at 25,000 ft after her oxygen mask disconnects. Which type of hypoxia is this?
explanation: Reduced inspired PO2 at altitude lowers alveolar PO2, which is hypoxic hypoxia.
noteA: Correct: the cause is low PO2.
noteB: Wrong: this is reduced oxygen-carrying capacity (anemia or CO).
noteC: Wrong: this is reduced perfusion (e.g. high G).
noteD: Wrong: this is impaired cellular use (e.g. cyanide).
